source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide whether a diet is balanced by checking for all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amounts for growth and development, while allowing needs to vary with age.
node_labels: Living systems: organisms, health and ecosystems

mx.teacher_note: A child and a grandparent require exactly the same types and amounts of nutrients.

intelligence.enrichment: A balanced diet has all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amount for proper growth and development, and nutrient requirements may vary according to age. right amounts of essential nutrients, roughage, and water matched to need -> balanced diet for proper growth and development The learner correctly applies this rule: A balanced diet has all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amount for proper growth and development, and nutrient requirements may vary according to age. A diet is balanced if it fills the stomach or has many food items, even without checking roughage, water, or age needs.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Mindful eating: a path to a healthy body. The student must decide: Decide whether a diet is balanced by checking for all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amounts for growth and development, while allowing needs to vary with age. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. Recalculate the key; do not copy source.key. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list.
